extra.message: NoSQL injection / authentication bypass in the /login route. username and password come straight from req.body and the string type-check (lines 54-56) is commented out, so an attacker can send object selectors such as {"$ne": null} for username/password. These are passed directly into User.findOne({ username, password }), letting an attacker log in as any user without knowing the password (MongoDB query operator injection).

Hardcoded JWT signing secret "secretkey" used both to sign tokens (line 64) and verify them (line 76). Because the key ships in the source, any attacker who reads the code can forge a valid JWT for an arbitrary user._id and impersonate any account on /protected, defeating authentication.

User passwords are stored and compared in plaintext. /register saves password as-is (line 40) and /login compares it via User.findOne({ username, password }) (line 58). bcryptjs is declared in package.json but never used, so a database leak exposes every account's raw password.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

extra.message: Hardcoded secrets shipped to the browser bundle: API key 'SUPER_SECRET_API_KEY_12345', admin username/password ('admin'/'SuperSecretDBPassword!') and JWT secret 'VERY_INSECURE_JWT_SECRET'. These are public to any visitor and are used for client-side login/authorization in Auth.jsx, Login.jsx and Profile.jsx.
DOM-based XSS: user-controlled comment text is concatenated into an HTML string and assigned to commentNode.innerHTML. An attacker can submit which executes when the comment is appended.
XSS via dangerouslySetInnerHTML: output state is set directly from user input (line 10 / line 73) and rendered as raw HTML, so an injected payload such as executes in the page.
DOM-based XSS: user-controlled HTML payload is written via document.getElementById('dynamic').innerHTML = output, allowing script execution through event-handler attributes.
XSS via dangerouslySetInnerHTML: userInput (from the input field) is rendered directly as HTML, so payloads like <script>alert('XSS');</script> execute when rendered.
DOM-based XSS: user comment is interpolated into HTML and set via innerHTML, enabling script execution when the comment node is appended.
XSS via dangerouslySetInnerHTML: dynamicContent is derived from user inputText (line 20) and rendered as raw HTML, executing injected markup.
DOM-based XSS: attacker-supplied payload is written to innerHTML of the 'injectedButton' element (e.g. ), executing in the victim's session.

Stored XSS: attacker-controlled data saved to localStorage (line 34) is read back in useEffect and rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML, so a stored payload fires every time the page loads for any user who shares/loads that storage.

Open redirect: the 'redirect' query-string parameter is assigned to redirectUrl (line 16) without any validation and later assigned to window.location.href, so an attacker can send victims to a phishing site (e.g. /redirect?redirect=https://evil.com).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: Broken access control / client-side enforced authorization: 'protected' data is gated only by comparing localStorage 'authToken' against Config.JWT_SECRET, a hardcoded value shipped in the public JS bundle. Any user can set localStorage.setItem('authToken', 'VERY_INSECURE_JWT_SECRET') and retrieve the protected data — the check is trivially bypassed.

Broken access control: profile data exposure is gated only by localStorage 'authToken' equalling the public hardcoded Config.JWT_SECRET, so the check can be bypassed trivially to reveal the hardcoded admin username and secret string.

Authentication is performed entirely client-side against hardcoded credentials (Config.USERNAME / Config.PASSWORD, visible in src/config.js), and the JWT secret is stored in localStorage (line 13). The credentials and secret are public in the bundle, so the login gate and 'authToken' both offer no real security.

Login relies on hardcoded credentials from config.js (admin / SuperSecretDBPassword!) and then stores the public JWT secret into localStorage as 'authToken'. Anyone can read the constants from the bundle and bypass the check or forge the stored token.

Client-side prototype pollution: mergeSettings copies every enumerable key of an attacker-controlled JSON payload onto the user object without an own-property / '__proto__' guard (line 15), and handleExploit merges the raw parsed payload (line 26). A payload like {"__proto__": {"isAdmin": true}} pollutes the object prototype, letting an attacker escalate privileges (isAdmin/premiumAccess) or tamper with object behavior.

cwe: CWE-1321: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution')

extra.message: Hardcoded API key 'API_KEY_LEAK_12345' is embedded in client code and appended to the query string of an external request (line 9: http://example-api.com/data?apiKey=${API_KEY}). The key is exposed to every visitor and also leaks over unencrypted HTTP and into server logs.
